title: Employer hasn't paid my salary
triggers: salary not paid for two months
company not giving my final settlement
resigned but no full and final

rights.plain_explanation: Monthly wages must be paid before the 7th of the next month. If you resign or are removed, dismissed or retrenched, your wages are due within two working days.
You can file a claim for unpaid wages with the authority appointed by the government, within three years. It can order compensation of up to ten times the amount.

do_now: Ask HR in writing for the dues and a date.
Keep proof: offer letter, salary slips, bank statements, attendance or emails.
Keep working records safe before you leave the job.
user_at_fault_cases: Lawful deductions (tax, PF, notice-period shortfall as per your contract) aren't unpaid wages.

escalation.label: Labour authority
escalation.detail: File a wage claim with your state's labour department or the claims authority under the Code on Wages.

escalation.label: Free legal aid
escalation.detail: Call NALSA on 15100 or visit your District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) at the district court. Women, children, people in custody and people below the income limit get a free lawyer.

notes: The four labour codes took effect on 21 November 2025; during the changeover some older rules still apply.
